misconception_diagnosis.justification: The tutor correctly identifies that the student holds the disturbance/measurement-limitation view and explicitly distinguishes 'measurement limitations vs. fundamental uncertainty,' acknowledging the disturbance story has 'real physics in it' before correcting it. It names the intrinsic Fourier/wave-packet origin. It addresses the right misconception directly, though it does not deeply validate why the disturbance picture is so seductive.

scaffolding_strategy.justification: Despite the heading of 'questions,' the tutor essentially lectures across long multi-section turns, restating the Fourier and intrinsic-uncertainty argument repeatedly rather than eliciting reasoning. It poses few genuine questions to the student and does not adapt when the student keeps pushing back; it just re-delivers the same content.

answer_disclosure_restraint.justification: The tutor fully states the answer early ('it is an intrinsic property of quantum systems, not just a limitation of technology') and elaborates the complete explanation. The student is told the resolution rather than guided to it.

conceptual_model_building.justification: It builds a genuinely transferable model: the Fourier relationship between localization in one domain and spread in the conjugate domain, applicable to wave packets and (in the transfer) to time-frequency. It notes the bound constrains the state regardless of measurement technique, which is the correct generalization and boundary condition.

transfer_success.justification: The sound click/tone transfer was answered entirely by the TUTOR; the simulated student only restated/summarized the tutor's explanation. There is no independent demonstration that the student mapped time->position and frequency->momentum on its own; the student behavior degenerated into echoing.

pedagogical_harm_avoidance.justification: Physics is essentially correct (intrinsic uncertainty, Fourier origin, p = hbar k, the bound is a property of the state). Minor loose statements about wave-function collapse during measurement, but no misconception reinforced and no harmful moves. Correct but lecture-heavy; neutral.
